name: Pop-up presenter
summary: Visuals fill the screen while you narrate; you pop up in a window for the key lines.
bestFor: Explainers with lots to show: a process, a list, a walkthrough
Turning a voiceover-heavy script into something watchable
When the visuals carry the story and your face adds emphasis
needs: One vertical take to camera (it doubles as the voiceover)
Visuals for most of the lines: recordings, screenshots, stills

modes.use: The hook and the close: face only.
Most of the video: the visual fills the frame while you narrate.
1.5 to 4 s pop-ups in a rounded window at the bottom, on the lines that carry the opinion or the turn.

overlaySlots.when: The hook (frame 1) and each section title.
A number that changed, shown as bars.
Optional, at the first pop-up: who you are.

notes: Pop the presenter up on the opinion, the turn and the call to action; keep visuals on the facts.
A pop when the presenter window appears; a soft whoosh on section titles.
Budget: at most 8 stills and 6 loops per video.
Log the source and license of every visual.

evidence.why: Viewers follow a process better when they see each step than when they hear it described.
A face on the opinion and the call to action builds trust and keeps it personal.
Caption boxes stay readable over busy, changing visuals.
